heading: IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE IN BITUNG CITY
translated_text:
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE IN BITUNG CITY

BITUNG CITY

NUMBER 8 OF 2019

MAYOR OF BITUNG

NORTH SULAWESI PROVINCE

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF BITUNG CITY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Bitung.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bitung.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the DPRD of the City of Bitung.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in the Region.
6. Woman is a person who has the female sex from birth or based on a court decision who is over 18 years of age.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child in the womb.
8. Act of violence is any act that results in suffering or pain physically, psychologically, sexually and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or pain, either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an action, deed, activity that includes prevention of acts of violence against women and children, handling services, assistance, recovery, reunification, empowerment of women and rehabilitation of child victims of acts of violence, carried out by the Regional Government, parents, husband, family or community, including therein the Integrated Service Center.
11. Prevention is a process, method, act to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Handling is a process, method, act to handle women and child victims as a result of acts of violence.
13. Assistance and recovery is all activities in order to assist and restore the physical, psychological condition and health disorders of women and child victims of acts of violence.
14. Reunification is an activity in order to reunite women and child victims of acts of violence with parents and/or family.
15. Empowerment is a process, method and act to empower women victims of acts of violence.
16. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that child victims of acts of violence can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Parent/guardian is biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother or guardian based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is various institutions that provide services for victims of violence, such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Centre Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter and the like.
21. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is the foundation and guideline for related regional apparatus, vertical agencies and the community in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of acts of violence.

heading: Article 2
Article 3
Article 4
CHAPTER II
Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) letter a is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

heading: Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) letter b is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

heading: Article 8
Article 9
Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts without the consent of women and children who become victims of exploitation, including but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits, whether physical/material in nature or non-physical/non-material; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of women and children who become victims of exploitation to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

heading: CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

General

heading: Article 11
Article 12
Article 13
Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

Family as referred to in Article 11 letter c has full responsibility to protect women and children from all forms of acts of violence.

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

Parents as referred to in Article 11 letter d have full responsibility to protect women and children from all forms of acts of violence.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence

heading: Article 16
CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

IMPLEMENTATION OF PREVENTION OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN

heading: Article 17
Article 18
Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. Forms of prevention of violence against women and children carried out by PPT, can be implemented through:
a. socialization activities of laws and regulations related to protection of women's and children's rights to the community; and
b. training of PPT members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing acts of violence against women and children.
2. PPT in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with competent parties in making efforts to prevent violence against women and children.
3. Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated in Mayor Regulation.

heading: Article 20
Article 21
Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

Parents have the responsibility to prevent acts of violence against women and children, including:
a. fostering love, affection and mutual respect within the family;
b. providing assistance to victims; and
c. reporting every form of domestic violence.

heading: Article 23
Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

Provisions regarding the form and procedures for preventing acts of violence against women and children shall be further regulated in a Mayoral Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

PROVISION OF SERVICES, ASSISTANCE AND RECOVERY FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN WHO ARE VICTIMS OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE

heading: Article 25
Article 26
Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

1. Handling of children who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 25 is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Provisions regarding the form and procedures for handling children who are victims of acts of violence shall be further regulated in a Mayoral Regulation.

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

1. Assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 25 are provided to women and children who are domiciled in the Region and who experience violence within the territory of the Region.
2. Forms of assistance and recovery services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in the form of:
a. women's empowerment;
b. child rehabilitation;
c. complaint, consultation and counseling services; and
d. assistance services.
3. Provisions regarding the form and procedures for assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence shall be further regulated in a Mayoral Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

INSTITUTIONS

Part One

Establishment of PPT

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

The provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence is carried out by the Regional Government by establishing PPT.

heading: Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

1. The provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence is carried out in an integrated manner by PPT.
2. In addition to the provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence, PPT takes preventive action against acts of violence against women and children.
3. PPT reports the implementation of the provision of handling, assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence as well as preventive action against acts of violence against women and children to the Mayor through the Agency.

heading: Article 31
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

PPT Counseling Division

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

1. PPT has a counseling division in assistance and recovery services for women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
2. The counseling division as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:
a. legal division;
b. health division;
c. spiritual division; and
d. psychology division.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Service Mechanism for Handling, Assistance and Recovery

heading: Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

1. PPT may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.
2. PPT provides services and temporary protection in the form of Safe Houses.
3. In the event that PPT does not yet have a Safe House, women and children who are victims of acts of violence are referred to PPT that has a Safe House.

heading: Article 34
Article 35
translated_text:
Article 35

Further provisions regarding the Standard Operating Procedures for Service Mechanisms for Handling, Assistance and Recovery of PPT shall be regulated in a Mayor Regulation.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Service Mechanism for Assistance and Recovery by Persons and/or Institutions Cooperating with PPT

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

Assistance shall be carried out by persons and/or institutions cooperating with PPT.

heading: Article 37
Article 38
translated_text:
Article 38

1. PPT shall report the implementation of protection provision for women and children who are victims of acts of violence to the Mayor through the Agency.
2. The reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
4. The submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

REUNIFICATION

Article 39

In order to return women and children who are victims of acts of violence to their families, the Regional Government shall be obligated to:
a. provide transportation costs and other needs for women and children who are victims of acts of violence to return home to their families;
b. provide and finance accompanying personnel to return women and children who are victims of acts of violence to their families; and
c. coordinate with the Government, Regional Government of the place of residence of women and children who are victims of acts of violence and the Indonesian National Police to return women and children who are victims of acts of violence to their families.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

EMPOWERMENT AND REHABILITATION

Article 40

1. Empowerment of women who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 16 paragraph (1) letter d shall be carried out by means of:
a. job training; and/or
b. facilitating the establishment of productive economic enterprises and joint business groups.
2. Job training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall coordinate with Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of manpower.
3. Job training for women who are victims of acts of violence may be carried out at job training institutions organized by the Regional Government or organized by the private sector.
4. The establishment of productive economic enterprises and joint business groups as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out in coordination with Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of small and medium enterprises.

heading: Article 41
CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 42

1. The Regional Government shall conduct guidance and supervision of the provision of protection for women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

heading: Article 43
translated_text:
Article 43

Guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 42 paragraph (1) shall be conducted in order to realize the objectives of providing protection for women and children who are victims of acts of violence in accordance with minimum service standards established by laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

FINANCING

Article 44

Costs required for the implementation of tasks in providing protection for women and children from acts of violence may be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 45
translated_text:
Article 45

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations and universities that carry out protection for women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be adjusted to the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 46

Implementing regulations of this Regional Regulation shall be established no later than 6 (six) months from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

heading: Article 47
translated_text:
Article 47

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Bitung City.

Enacted in Bitung on 21 October 2019

MAYOR OF BITUNG,

MAXIMILIAAN JONAS LOMBAN

Promulgated in Bitung on 21 October 2019

AUDY RONALD RICHARD PANGEMANAN

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BITUNG CITY

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BITUNG CITY

NUMBER 8 YEAR 2019 CONCERNING PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE IN BITUNG CITY

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BITUNG CITY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Bitung City as one of the areas that has become a center of economic activity in North Sulawesi has attracted many people from outside the City area to work in various industrial sectors that exist. Although this has a positive effect on the economic sector, but viewed from the security and order side, it will greatly affect the increased risk of the emergence of security disturbances, especially for those that threaten women and children as vulnerable parties.

The Regional Government, which sees this as a potential threat that must be resolved, then established this Regional Regulation as a solution to the problem of security threats that arise for women and children. In this Regional Regulation, the form of protection provided by the Regional Government and various parties involved therein is regulated so as to reduce the high security threats to women and children in Bitung City, in addition, institutional arrangements are also regulated that will ensure the implementation of holistic protection so that each party will know its duties at each stage of protection carried out by the Regional Government.
